input.title: Move LH-02 from DF-1310-05 to TP-1310-04 to cover high-grade loading until LH-07 is repaired

options.description: No reaction. TP-1310-04 (8.4 g/t, priority 1) is not loaded from 09:18 to 17:00 (7.7 h).
Hold and resume when LH-07 is back at 14:30 (PR-0001 likely, 5 h). Low case 13:30 puts 129 t / 34.8 oz at risk. High case 16:30 puts 216 t / 58.3 oz at risk.

Move LH-02 from DF-1310-05 (5.2 g/t, same level 1310, 0.5 h move). It loads 1310-04 from about 10:00 to 14:30 and then returns by about 15:00. Residual risk is 21 t / 5.7 oz at 1310-04 before it arrives, plus 110 t / 18.4 oz lost at DF-1310-05. Total at risk is 131 t / 24.1 oz. Alternatives: LH-04 from TP-1220-01 (3.9 g/t, 1220, assumed 1.0 h move) nets about 18.8 oz, but that is within the error of my move-time assumption and it idles drill PP-05. LH-11 from TP-1250-02 nets about 16.6 oz. LH-06 and LH-10 (6.8 and 6.0 g/t) are worse.

input.calculation: Oz formula: oz = t x g/t / 31.1035. Productive window is 07:00-17:00 (10 h). LH-07 rate is 300 t / 10 h = 30 t/h. At 8.4 g/t that is 0.27006 oz/t, or 8.10 oz/h. do_nothing: 09:18 to 17:00 is 7.7 h, so 231 t and 62.4 oz. wait_for_repair: 09:18 to 14:30 is 5.2 h, so 156 t and 42.1 oz. reassign_loader with LH-02: LH-02 rate is 200 t / 10 h = 20 t/h at 5.2 g/t, which is 0.16719 oz/t or 3.34 oz/h. It leaves at about 09:30 and arrives about 10:00 (assumed 0.5 h, based on the 0.5 h activation of reserve places). It loads 10:00 to 14:30 = 4.5 h, so 135 t x 0.27006 = 36.5 oz protected. LH-02 is out of its stope from 09:30 to 15:00 (5.5 h including the return), so 110 t x 0.16719 = 18.4 oz lost. Net = 36.5 - 18.4 = 18.1 oz. Residual risk is 09:18 to 10:00 at 1310-04 (0.7 h = 21 t, 5.7 oz) plus 18.4 oz lost = 24.1 oz. That is 18.0 oz better than waiting (42.1 - 24.1), which matches the 18.1 net within rounding. Candidate nets, using the same method: LH-04 (1220, 18 t/h, 2.26 oz/h, assumed 1.0 h move) loads 4 h = 120 t / 32.4 oz and loses 6 h = 108 t / 13.6 oz, net about 18.8. LH-11 (1250, 20 t/h, 2.64 oz/h) loads 4 h = 32.4 oz and loses 6 h = 15.8 oz, net about 16.6. LH-02 is chosen over LH-04 because it is on the same level (shorter, more certain move) and does not idle drill PP-05. Its net is within 0.7 oz of LH-04's. If LH-07 returns at 13:30 or 16:30 the numbers change; the loader should return when LH-07 is confirmed back.

I don't know whether DF-1310-05 (a fill phase) has downstream dependencies. Check with the production supervisor.
Whether the 1310-04 access is clear while LH-07 is stuck there. Ask maintenance or dispatch.

I submitted action proposal PR-0002, which is waiting for human approval. It moves LH-02 from DF-1310-05 to TP-1310-04 to cover the 8.4 g/t stope while LH-07 is repaired. The plan assumes LH-07 is back at 14:30, per the maintenance assessment PR-0001.

| Option | Tonnes at risk | Oz at risk |
|---|---|---|
| Do nothing | 231 | 62.4 |
| Wait for repair | 156 | 42.1 |
| Reassign LH-02 | 131 | 24.1 |

The reassignment protects about 36.5 oz and loses about 18.4 oz at DF-1310-05, a net gain of about 18.1 oz.

The move time is my assumption: 0.5 h on the same level and 1.0 h across levels, based on how long the idle reserve places take to activate. LH-04 from TP-1220-01 nets about 18.8 oz, which is within the error of that assumption. I chose LH-02 because it is on the same level and doesn't idle drill PP-05. The diagnosis is also not confirmed, so I set confidence at 0.6.
